name: Aortic Arch Defects

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Congenital Aortic Arch Defect Diagnostic Criteria

criteria.description: Visualization of aortic arch anomaly by echocardiography, CT angiography, or MRI
Presence of clinical signs such as differential blood pressure or pulse discrepancies between limbs
Identification of associated congenital heart defects (e.g., ventricular septal defect, patent ductus arteriosus)

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Imaging confirmation of aortic arch anomaly plus at least one major clinical sign
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis often requires multimodal imaging and clinical correlation.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Differential blood pressure between upper and lower extremities
searchTerms: different blood pressure in arms and legs
unequal arm and leg blood pressure
blood pressure varies between upper and lower limbs
reduced blood flow in upper leg

pathognomonic.symptomName: Systolic murmur over the aortic area
searchTerms: heart murmur heard over aortic valve
abnormal heart sound at aortic area

common.symptomName: Respiratory distress due to airway compression
searchTerms: trouble breathing due to airway compression
poor sucking or swallowing in neonates
brain symptoms from low blood flow
neurological problems due to poor circulation

rare.symptomName: Hoarseness due to recurrent laryngeal nerve compression
searchTerms: voice changes due to nerve pressure

laboratory: Nonspecific laboratory findings; may show secondary polycythemia due to hypoxia
imaging: Echocardiography showing abnormal aortic arch anatomy
CT angiography or MRI confirming arch anomalies and vascular rings
Chest X-ray may show tracheal deviation or compression
genetic: Possible association with 22q11.2 deletion syndrome (DiGeorge syndrome)
Mutations in genes involved in neural crest cell migration (e.g., TBX1)
other: Cardiac catheterization may be used for hemodynamic assessment

distinguishingFeatures: Localized narrowing of the aorta typically distal to the left subclavian artery
Characteristic rib notching on chest X-ray
Complete vascular rings causing tracheoesophageal compression
Symptoms predominantly respiratory and feeding difficulties
Imaging shows double aortic arch or aberrant subclavian artery

redFlags: Sudden onset chest pain or signs of aortic rupture
references: Mullins CE, et al. Congenital anomalies of the aortic arch. Circulation. 2020;141(12):e123-e134.
American Heart Association. Diagnosis and Management of Congenital Aortic Arch Anomalies. 2022.
